Shift of the whole lactate curve between two tests

Source: R/compare.R
curve_shift.Rd

How far the fitted lactate curve moved between two tests: the intensity gained at each lactate value, and, when intensity is given, the lactate saved at each intensity. A rightward shift (more intensity for the same lactate) is the classic sign of better endurance; check the peak lactate too (see compare_tests()).

Usage

curve_shift(before, after, lactate = seq(1.5, 4, by = 0.5), intensity = NULL)

Arguments

before, after

The results of lactate_threshold() for the two tests, with the same sport.

lactate

Lactate values (mmol/L) at which to compare the intensity. Values outside either curve are NA. Defaults to seq(1.5, 4, by = 0.5).

intensity

Intensities at which to compare the lactate, or NULL.

Value

a tibble with lactate, intensity_before, intensity_after and shift; with intensity, rows with intensity, lactate_before, lactate_after and lactate_change are added.

Examples

series <- subset(lactate_tests, athlete == "cyclist_series")
before <- lactate_threshold(subset(series, day == 0), intensity, lactate, plot = FALSE)
after <- lactate_threshold(subset(series, day == 58), intensity, lactate, plot = FALSE)
curve_shift(before, after)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>   lactate intensity_before intensity_after shift
#>     <dbl>            <dbl>           <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1.5              262             283    20
#> 2     2                282             301    19
#> 3     2.5              296             316    19
#> 4     3                308             328    20
#> 5     3.5              318             338    20
#> 6     4                327             348    21
